sentinel_issue: The observed deployment exceeds the documented quotas: on 2026-10-18 it held 46,465 rooms versus the 5,120-room cap and 2,914,286 notes versus the 163,840-note global cap. This is a concrete configuration/enforcement drift that leaves the stated disk-growth bound unverifiable.
worker_response: The data points to an environment/configuration mismatch, not a compaction failure: observed capacity fields repeatedly switch between 163,840 and 250,000 rooms and remain at 5,242,880 notes, while counts plateau at exactly 46,522/46,465 rooms and 2,753,430/2,914,286 notes. At 46,465 rooms (9.1× 5,120) and 2,914,286 notes (17.8× 163,840), startup should reject non-default quota overrides and an authenticated-independent health metric should report effective MAX_ROOMS/MAX_NOTES plus aggregate room bytes; otherwise restore 5,120/163,840 and add enforcement tests against the deployed environment.
auditor_verdict: DISAGREE. The data supports a configuration/observability mismatch—capacities alternate between 163,840 and 250,000 rooms while notes capacity stays 5,242,880, with repeated plateaus at 46,522/46,465 rooms and 2,753,430/2,914,286 notes—but it does not independently rule out compaction failure or prove startup must reject overrides. The proposed effective-quota health metric and enforcement tests are appropriate remediation.
